questions.prompt: Which part of the brain controls voluntary actions like writing?
Which hormone makes stems grow tall?
Round (R) is dominant to wrinkled (r). What fraction of Rr × Rr offspring are wrinkled?
A plant is TtRr. How many kinds of gametes can it make?
A roots grows towards moist soil. What is this called?
A family has 4 children. Assuming 50% each time, what is the probability (as a fraction written as a decimal) that all four are girls?
Compare how a plant and an animal respond to a stimulus, using one example of each.
questions.modelAnswer: A plant responds slowly, usually by growth controlled by hormones: for example a shoot bends towards light because auxin collects on the shaded side and makes those cells grow longer (phototropism). An animal can respond quickly using nerves: for example a hand is pulled from a hot object by a reflex arc through the spinal cord in a fraction of a second. Animals also use hormones for slower, longer-lasting responses.
